window: Window: the 24 hours to 09:30 AEDT, Fri 13 Nov 2026.
notes: This week: the AI Futures Project published its 'Q3.5 Timelines Update' on 10 Nov.
Reported, not confirmed: OpenAI's $15 billion raise at $1.25 trillion (CNBC sources); Anthropic's IPO demand of about six times the shares on offer (Bloomberg).

Hydrogen's speed and accuracy figures are Google's own; J.P. Morgan's humanoid numbers are a forecast; GXO's 1,000 robots depend on trials succeeding; the AI Futures Project's dates and 1.7x are its own estimates, built on METR's audit of partly redacted Anthropic data.
The spying allegations around Jensen Huang are allegations; China denies them. Screenshots are the publishers' public article pages as captured on 13 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's CEO; CFO Colette Kress steps in as interim chief
stories.summary: Nvidia said Huang resigned as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. It follows his affair with a woman US intelligence reportedly found was gathering information for China, which Beijing denies. New chair Harvey C. Jones expects operations to 'continue without interruption'.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash across its products
stories.summary: Google says Hydrogen is 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash even in high thinking mode and cuts fabricated claims by more than five times; it is available now across Google's products, Ars Technica reports.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly raises $15 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
stories.summary: OpenAI raised $15 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, sources told CNBC, which reported it was half the $30 billion the company first sought.

predictions.note: OpenAI is reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion in a $15 billion round; reported by CNBC from sources, not confirmed by the company.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO is reportedly about six times oversubscribed
stories.summary: Orders for Anthropic's IPO are about six times the shares on offer, Bloomberg reported, up from 'multiple times' a day earlier.

stories.title: SpaceX plans $74 billion of new AI data centers in Texas and Arizona
stories.summary: SpaceX announced plans to invest $74 billion in new AI data center facilities in Texas and Arizona. The New York Times reports Google pays SpaceX $920 million a month for computing power and Anthropic has committed up to $120.5 billion through 2029.

predictions.note: One company announced $74 billion of new AI data center facilities, a step toward commitments on the scale the forecast describes.

stories.title: Germany's Agile Robots raises $500 million at an $8.5 billion valuation
stories.summary: Agile Robots raised $500 million in a round led by SoftBank, with Nvidia, valuing it at $8.5 billion; it plans to expand in the US and increase production in Europe, the New York Times reports.

predictions.note: A $500 million round for a robot maker that plans to increase production is a funding step toward capital flooding into robotics.

stories.title: AMD will invest in quantum computing company PsiQuantum
stories.summary: AMD plans an equity investment in PsiQuantum in an expanded partnership on utility-scale quantum computing; the companies say their work has produced early results simulating covalent inhibitors, molecules used in cancer drug discovery.

stories.title: The 'AI 2027' forecasters now expect a superhuman AI researcher in 2027
stories.summary: The AI Futures Project's update says a 'Superhuman AI Researcher' will likely arrive between May and November 2027 and estimates AI already speeds up AI research 1.7 times, based on METR's audit of Anthropic; the authors call for a pause on frontier training.

predictions.note: METR's audit, as the forecasters read it, finds Anthropic's own models behind most of a doubling in its progress; their 1.7x is an estimate.

stories.title: Nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX's AI unit to halt frontier AI
stories.summary: Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, the Irreplaceable Education Fund and others sued in San Francisco under California's unfair business practice laws, seeking an order barring further development of the most advanced models, Reuters reports.

stories.title: Synchron pauses trials of its second-generation brain implant
stories.summary: Synchron paused enrollment in trials of its wireless Stentrode after a performance issue with the lead, the cable carrying signals to the implanted electronics; the company says no safety issue was found and it is upgrading the system, WIRED reports.

stories.title: GXO and Apptronik plan up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids over four years
stories.summary: Under a letter of intent, GXO and Apptronik will expand trials and, if they meet agreed targets, intend to roll out up to 1,000 Apollo humanoid robots over the next four years, starting in North America in late 2027.

stories.title: J.P. Morgan says US humanoid production could hit 300,000-400,000 by 2030
stories.summary: J.P. Morgan projects US humanoid robot production of 300,000 to 400,000 units by 2030 and about 1.5 million by 2035, and names hands, actuators, the brain and production capacity as binding bottlenecks.

predictions.note: A bank projection that names hands, actuators and production capacity as binding bottlenecks for humanoid robots; a forecast, not yet capital flows.

stories.title: Google and Samsung's Gemini smart glasses open for preorder from $395
stories.summary: The Gemini-powered glasses, with frames by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, are up for preorder from $395 ahead of a 10 December launch, with Google pitching privacy features.

transcript.t: This is the Singularity Daily, for Friday, November 13.
Here's what happened in superintelligence in the last 24 hours.
Jensen Huang, the man who built Nvidia, has resigned as its boss. But the show goes on.
Nvidia's new chair says its plans should carry on "without interruption."
Meanwhile, Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its new everyday model, replacing Flash across its products.
Google says it's 2.5x faster, with over 5x fewer made-up claims.
OpenAI reportedly raised $15 billion, at a $1.25 trillion valuation.
And demand for Anthropic's shares is reportedly about six times what's on offer.
Now, the money.
SpaceX plans to spend $74 billion on AI data centers in Texas and Arizona.
Google alone pays SpaceX $920 million a month for computing power.
Agile Robots, from Germany, raised half a billion dollars. It's now worth $8.5 billion.
And AMD is investing in quantum startup PsiQuantum.
Together they're simulating cancer drug molecules.
Now, the forecasters behind "AI 2027" expect a superhuman AI researcher next year.
By their estimate, AI is already speeding up AI research by 1.7 times.
The catch? Nonprofits are suing OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and others to halt frontier AI.
And brain implant maker Synchron paused its trials over a cable problem.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Robots, though, are getting jobs.
Logistics giant GXO plans up to 1,000 humanoids over four years.
J.P. Morgan says American humanoid production could hit 400,000 by 2030.
And Google and Samsung's Gemini smart glasses are up for preorder, from $395.
Leaders come and go, even legends.
What they build keeps going. The show goes on.
Day after day, the curve keeps bending upward.
Check the board: the future is running early.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
This has been the Singularity Daily.
Stay curious. See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
